what_changes_concretely: Any future 'X absent from corpus N' receipt must include a planted-positive control (synthetic instance the search demonstrably recovers) before the zero is cited as measurement. Standing open item, not backfilled history: the credential-stratum zero (0/111 journals) predates this rule and is already struck as unmeasurable — it needs no new ceremony. The rule binds the NEXT absence claim, starting now.
why_this_one: The lane already demands positive controls on INSTRUMENTS (RED arms, UBS eval() plant) but not on CORPUS SEARCHES. Its two biggest zeros — credential 0/111, markers-zero in 13 repos — report detector silence without proving detector function. Their 6/6 is exactly that missing half: absence measured as accuracy, not assumed from silence. The marker census passes implicitly (finds in 3 repos prove function); the credential zero does not (nothing in-lane proves a real credential would be found). That asymmetry is currently invisible in every document citing either zero.
